_comment: Effect lines from a distinct section (v390). After v389, 80 pairs still printed nothing. This pass reopened the 52 silent only because a sibling line was judged to cover the act’s only change on the issue (`category: "sibling"`) or the act was judged to have no bearing on it (`"unrelated"`), and searched the whole bill for a separate requirement or prohibition on that issue that no line on the same act already states. Utah text is the bill at `textFrom` with `[-…-]` for struck and `[+…+]` for inserted text; only a change the bill makes counts. Federal text is the engrossed or enrolled bill on GovInfo; the twelve House amendments have no text there and are read from their stored purpose. `siblingLines` is every line the act already printed, by issue, when the pass ran; `distinctFrom` says why the new line is a different change. Every `terms` phrase is in the quoted text and the line; every other content word is in that text, the title, a `plain` restatement or an effect verb; every qualifier in `bounds` stays in the line. The other 28 (`notReopened`) were confirmed silent after a body read, already read by v386, carry a status conflict, are a forecast or confirmation, or have no vote row, and were not reopened. Lines are stored once in consistency.js _DOS_EFFECT under the EFFECT DISTINCT SECTION SLICE 19 marker. No score, weight, mapping or key is read from or written to here.

rows.title: Sex-based Designations for Privacy, Anti-bullying, and Women's Opportunities
rows.priorWhy: The privacy in this bill is physical privacy in restrooms, showers, and locker rooms; nothing in the provisions concerns personal data or Big Tech.

siblingLines.lgbtq_rights: Set a legal standard for sex-based distinctions in certain public settings and applied it to sex-designated restrooms and locker rooms.

rows.provisions: This bill: defines terms; defines certain terms for the entire Utah Code; establishes a legal standard for distinctions on the basis of sex in certain publicly owned or controlled circumstances; establishes acceptable and prohibited distinctions on the basis of sex; enacts provisions regarding sex-designated restroom, shower, or locker room facilities that students use within the public education system; requires local education agencies to establish a privacy plan with parents and students in certain cases to address gender identity and fear of bullying; enacts provisions regarding sex-designated shower or locker room facilities where the general public has an expectation of privacy; establishes components of the crimes of voyeurism and criminal trespass for certain actions within a covered sex-designated shower or locker room; requires government entities to: report allegations of certain criminal offenses to law enforcement; adopt a privacy compliance plan; provide a single-occupant facility in new construction; and consider the feasibility of certain retrofit or remodel projects; provides indemnification for government entities for certain claims; requires the state auditor to investigate government entity compliance with certain requirements; requires the attorney general to impose fines on political subdivisions that fail to cure noncompliance that the state auditor identifies; amends certain crimes to establish a reasonable expectation of privacy in public restrooms, including enhanced penalties for: committing multiple offenses concurrently within a public restroom, shower, or locker room; and committing certain offenses within a public restroom, shower, or locker room that is designated for the opposite sex; enacts a criminal offense for loitering in a restroom, shower, or locker room where the general public has an expectation of privacy; establishes elements of the crime of emergency reporting abuse for making repeated false reports alleging a violation of a sex-designation in a publicly owned or controlled shower or locker room facility where the general public has an expectation of privacy; and makes technical and conforming changes.
rows.why: Searched the full bill for data, records, recording and electronic provisions; the changes concern physical privacy in restrooms and locker rooms, including voyeurism penalties there; nothing on personal data or Big Tech.

rows.provisions: This bill: defines terms; clarifies how a school responds when a student refrains from participation in school due to a student's or a student's parent's religious belief or right of conscience, consistent with Utah Constitution, Article I, Section 4; grants the State Board of Education rulemaking authority; and makes technical and conforming changes.
rows.why: Read both sections; the parent waiver in 53G-10-205(4) and parent notice are the same religious/conscience opt-out already stated on the religious_liberty line, differing only in who invokes it; nothing gives parents say over curriculum content or materials.

rows.title: School Absenteeism Amendments
rows.priorWhy: The issue is funding schools and raising teacher pay; the provisions only direct absenteeism strategies and duties, with no funding or pay change.
rows.provisions: This bill: directs local education agencies to include certain evidence-based strategies for children as part of their efforts to reduce student absenteeism; enacts new duties for the State Board of Education with respect to addressing chronic absenteeism prevention and intervention; and amends the responsibilities of the Division of Juvenile Justice and Youth Services to require the use of evidence-informed and research-informed interventions.
rows.why: Read all sections; changes direct absenteeism interventions and state board duties; no funding, appropriation or teacher pay change.

rows.title: Technology Commercialization Amendments
rows.priorWhy: The only provision tied to this issue is the Utah innovation fund investing in technology commercialization, which the tech_innovation line already states; nothing touches regulation or taxes.

siblingLines.tech_innovation: Required the Utah Innovation Lab to run the Utah innovation fund for investing in businesses developed through technology commercialization.

rows.provisions: This bill: enacts the Utah Innovation Lab Act; defines terms; creates the Utah Innovation Lab (innovation lab) and provides for the innovation lab's powers and purposes; establishes a board to govern the innovation lab and provides for the board membership, terms, and responsibilities, and provides certain limits on board members; requires the innovation lab to organize and administer the Utah innovation fund for the purpose of investing in businesses developed in the state through technology commercialization; provides for the Utah innovation fund's powers and purposes; and requires the innovation lab to comply with certain audit and reporting requirements.
rows.why: Read all seven enacted sections and the appropriation: board, fund, investment purposes, report and audit duties and a $15,000,000 one-time appropriation; no section cuts a regulation or a tax, so nothing beyond the tech_innovation fund line bears on deregulation.

rows.title: Public Education Compliance
rows.priorWhy: The provisions set board compliance, complaint and publication duties and data-reporting duties for districts; nothing in them funds schools or raises teacher pay, and the publication duty is already stated on the transparency line.

siblingLines.gov_transparency: Required the State Board of Education to post meeting information on its website and use a compliance framework for noncompliance.

rows.provisions: This bill: requires the state board to: use an existing compliance framework to address reports or allegations of noncompliance; develop a system to address complaints to the Utah Professional Practices Advisory Commission in a timely and expedient manner; and publish information related to state board meetings on the state board's website; may require the state board to issue a report; requires a school district or charter school to provide information to the state board that is necessary for the state board to fulfill a statutory data gathering, compliance, or reporting requirement; and makes technical and conforming changes.
rows.why: Checked every insert and strike: compliance procedures and remedies (including reimbursement instead of future allocations), vote-record posting, UPPAC complaints, and district/charter data duties; none raises teacher pay or funds schools or classrooms.

rows.title: Judicial Retention Changes
rows.priorWhy: The provisions create a legislative committee to evaluate state judges for retention; they say nothing about courts checking executive action, which is what this issue covers.
rows.provisions: This bill: modifies the ballot requirements for judicial retention elections; modifies the information contained in the voter information pamphlet for judicial retention elections; requires the lieutenant governor to transmit a retention recommendation from the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance to a county clerk; amends the ballot language for a judicial retention election to address a retention recommendation from the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance; provides that certain records for the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance are private; requires the Judicial Conduct Committee to provide records to the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance under certain conditions; defines terms related to judicial performance evaluations; requires the Judicial Performance Evaluation Commission to provide the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance with a list of judges who are subject to a retention election in the next scheduled regular general election; creates the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance; addresses the membership, length of appointment, selection of the chairs, quorum requirements, and compensation for the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance; allows the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance to evaluate a judge and provide a recommendation to the public as to whether the judge should be retained for another term; provides the evaluation and recommendation process for the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance, including requiring the Joint Legislative Committee on Judicial Performance to: hold any committee meeting to evaluate a judge before August 15 of the year in which the judge is subject to a retention election in a regular general election; and provide a retention recommendation for a judge to the lieutenant governor on or before August 15 of the year in which the judge is subject to a retention election in a regular general election; and makes technical and conforming changes.
rows.why: The body amends 78A-12-206 (a public education campaign on judicial performance evaluations) plus a $14,400 appropriation; it concerns state judge retention and says nothing about courts halting executive action.

rows.title: Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Amendments
rows.priorWhy: The provisions cover probation standards, debt collection, pretrial release procedure and restitution; none funds police or raises penalties for violent crime.

siblingLines.tough_on_crime: Let the Office of State Debt Collection collect a civil judgment of restitution and extended garnishments to wages held by a third party.

rows.provisions: This bill: requires that counties offering probation services adopt certain probation standards and practices; modifies definitions; provides that the Office of State Debt Collection has the authority to collect civil accounts receivable or a civil judgment of restitution and interest thereon; provides that administrative garnishments also apply to a debtor's property or wages that are under control of a third party; requires the Office of State Debt Collection to provide an accounting of the unpaid balance of a defendant's criminal accounts receivable at the time of termination of the defendant's sentence; provides repayment procedures for any unpaid balance of a defendant's criminal accounts receivable upon termination of a sentence; provides circumstances that constitute a material change in circumstances; adds requirements for temporary pretrial status orders of detention; modifies provisions relating to factors for pretrial release requirements; provides that a request for a pretrial release at an initial appearance does not constitute a pretrial detention hearing; requires a court to make findings of fact when making a determination regarding pretrial release; adds a financial condition schedule to aid a court in determining the amount of a fixed financial condition; requires a judge to take certain actions if the judge is unable to hold a pretrial detention hearing before a certain deadline; provides for required procedures when a no bail hold is requested; provides that certain Board of Pardons and Parole decisions on restitution are final and not subject to judicial review; codifies order of restitution procedures that apply to certain offenders sentenced before July 1, 2021; provides procedures for the accounting and payment of restitution owed to various state governmental entities; permits a sentencing court to authorize the deposit of funds in certain interest-bearing accounts when distribution to a victim is pending; permits the Board of Pardons and Parole to order recovery of fees incurred on behalf of a sentenced offender in addition to the existing ability to recover costs; makes coordinating modifications related to docket entry and interest assessments; permits a court to set restitution for a juvenile sentenced to prison; includes a coordination clause that requires changes to a section of this bill supersede the changes to that section in H.B. 312, Criminal Justice Amendments; and makes technical and grammatical changes.
rows.why: Read probation, debt collection, pretrial and restitution changes; the closest is detention keyed to habitual offender status and a bail schedule, which are pretrial rules, not police funding or tougher penalties for violent crime.

rows.title: Drug Sentencing Modifications
rows.priorWhy: The bill’s only operative provision is the required indeterminate prison term for armed drug distribution, which the tough_on_crime line states; the provisions contain no separate sentencing-reform change.

siblingLines.tough_on_crime: Required, with certain exceptions, an indeterminate prison term for distributing drugs with a dangerous weapon readily accessible.

rows.provisions: This bill: requires a court, with certain exceptions, to sentence an individual convicted of distributing drugs to an indeterminate prison term if the individual, while distributing the drugs, intentionally or knowingly: had a dangerous weapon readily accessible for immediate use; or distributed a firearm or possessed a firearm with intent to distribute the firearm; and makes technical and conforming changes.
rows.why: The struck one-year consecutive firearm term in 58-37-8(1)(c) is replaced in the same subsection by the required indeterminate prison term the tough_on_crime line states; a line saying only that the term was struck would read as lighter sentencing, which the subsection as a whole does not do.

rows.title: Directing the President pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities in Lebanon.
rows.priorWhy: The rationale's one effect, removing U.S. forces from hostilities in Lebanon, is what the act's restraint line already says; the rest only describes a yea's direction. (Recorded in db/vr-blank-rows-slice10.json; reread against the measure’s text on file, which changes nothing here.)

siblingLines.restraint: Would have directed U.S. forces out of any hostilities in Lebanon within seven days; the House rejected it 189-235.
siblingLines.war_powers: Would have invoked the War Powers Resolution on Lebanon hostilities absent congressional authorization; the House rejected it 189-235.

rows.why: Read all three sections: the only operative clause is the 7-day removal from Lebanon hostilities (restraint/war_powers lines); Secs. 2-3 are rules of construction preserving security cooperation and denying authorization, not separate requirements.

rows.title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.
rows.priorWhy: The rationale's one effect, removing U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran absent authorization, is what the act's iran_policy and restraint lines already say; the rest only describes a yea's direction. (Recorded in db/vr-blank-rows-slice10.json; reread against the measure’s text on file, which changes nothing here.)

siblingLines.iran_policy: Directs the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran, keeping self-defense; the House agreed to it 214-208.
siblingLines.restraint: Would direct U.S. forces out of Iran hostilities, keeping self-defense and intelligence sharing; the House agreed to it 214-208.
siblingLines.war_powers: Would invoke the War Powers Resolution against hostilities with Iran absent congressional authorization; the House agreed to it 214-208.

rows.why: Sec. 1(a) removal from Iran hostilities is already the iran_policy/restraint/war_powers lines; Sec. 1(b), 2 and 3 are rules of construction (self-defense, troop presence, intelligence sharing, no authorization) that siblings already note or that impose nothing.

rows.title: Unlocking our Domestic LNG Potential Act of 2025
rows.priorWhy: The rationale states an aim only ("Aims to grow U.S. energy exports"), not something the bill does. (Recorded in db/vr-blank-rows-slice9.json; reread against the measure’s text on file, which changes nothing here.)

siblingLines.energy_production: Would give FERC exclusive authority over natural gas export and import facilities and deem those exports and imports in the public interest.
siblingLines.permitting_reform: Would eliminate the Energy Department’s separate approval step and consolidate permitting at FERC.
siblingLines.climate_action: Would end the review stage at which the emissions and price effects of an export are weighed.

rows.why: Sec. 2 only moves export/import approval to FERC and deems it in the public interest (sibling lines); new subsection (d) is a savings clause keeping presidential sanctions authority, not a tariff or trade-rule change.

rows.title: Protecting American Energy Production Act
rows.priorWhy: the rationale's one fact, barring a federal fracking ban, is the enviro_energy line's own subject. (Recorded in db/vr-blank-rows-slice9.json; reread against the measure’s text on file, which changes nothing here.)

siblingLines.enviro_energy: Would bar a federal fracking moratorium to protect and expand domestic oil and gas production; the House passed it 226-188.
siblingLines.energy_production: Would bar the President from declaring a fracking moratorium unless an Act of Congress authorizes it; the House passed it 226-188.
siblingLines.states_federal_power: Would keep the decision with the states rather than Washington on regulating hydraulic fracturing; the House passed it 226-188.

rows.why: Sec. 2 has only a sense of Congress on state primacy and the bar on a presidential fracking moratorium absent an Act of Congress, both already the energy_production/states_federal_power lines; no regulatory-review or regulation-cutting provision.

rows.title: Protecting American Energy Production Act
rows.priorWhy: the rationale ("Concerns energy development on and under public and private lands") states a topic, not an effect. (Recorded in db/vr-blank-rows-slice9.json; reread against the measure’s text on file, which changes nothing here.)

siblingLines.enviro_energy: Would bar a federal fracking moratorium to protect and expand domestic oil and gas production; the House passed it 226-188.
siblingLines.energy_production: Would bar the President from declaring a fracking moratorium unless an Act of Congress authorizes it; the House passed it 226-188.
siblingLines.states_federal_power: Would keep the decision with the states rather than Washington on regulating hydraulic fracturing; the House passed it 226-188.

rows.why: The single operative clause (Sec. 2(b), no presidential fracking moratorium without an Act of Congress) is already the energy_production and enviro_energy lines; nothing else in the act touches resource development.

rows.title: HALT Fentanyl Act
rows.priorWhy: the rationale's one effect, permanent scheduling of fentanyl-related substances, is the immig_fentanyl line's own subject; the rest names a topic. (Recorded in db/vr-blank-rows-slice9.json; reread against the measure’s text on file, which changes nothing here.)

siblingLines.immig_fentanyl: Would toughen federal scheduling of fentanyl-related substances to fight the overdose crisis; the House passed it 312-108.
siblingLines.tough_on_crime: Would make Schedule I placement permanent and attach mandatory penalties; the House passed it 312-108.

rows.why: Checked Secs. 2-7: scheduling and penalties are the sibling lines; Sec. 3 streamlines Schedule I research registration, Sec. 4 fixes cross-references, Sec. 5 rulemaking; none expands mental-health or addiction treatment as such.

rows.title: Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act
rows.priorWhy: the rationale states only how a vote aligns with a position; its one fact, the sex-at-birth definition, is the edu_balance row's own subject. (Recorded in db/vr-blank-rows-slice9.json; reread against the measure’s text on file, which changes nothing here.)

siblingLines.lgbtq_rights: Would restrict transgender athletes’ participation in school and college sports for women and girls; the House passed it 218-206.
siblingLines.public_schools: Would apply to federally funded school and college athletic programs under Title IX; the House passed it 218-206.
siblingLines.edu_balance: Would set a federal rule for how sex is defined in school sports eligibility; the House passed it 218-206.

rows.why: Sec. 2 only sets the Title IX sports rule, sex definition, a training/practice carve-out and a GAO study; nothing gives parents a say over curriculum, library materials or instruction.

rows.title: Rescissions Act of 2025
rows.priorWhy: the rationale restates the $7.9 billion foreign-assistance rescission that the act's cut-spending and America First foreign policy lines already carry, so a line would borrow a sibling's fact. (Recorded in db/vr-blank-rows-slice9.json; reread against the measure’s text on file, which changes nothing here.)

siblingLines.america_first_fp: Rescinded about $7.9 billion in foreign-assistance balances, development aid among them; the House passed it 214-212, the Senate 51-48.
siblingLines.cut_spending: Cancelled unobligated balances for the State Department, USAID and public broadcasting; the House cleared it 214-212, the Senate 51-48.
siblingLines.gov_waste: Returned roughly $9 billion of enacted budget authority to the Treasury unspent; the House cleared it 214-212, the Senate 51-48.
siblingLines.national_debt: Reduced federal outlays by the rescinded balances, below the House’s $9.4 billion; the House cleared it 214-212, the Senate 51-48.
siblingLines.audit_spending: Codified DOGE-identified cuts through the Impoundment Control Act’s rescission process; the House cleared it 214-212, the Senate 51-48.
siblingLines.gov_services: Cut funding for public-media and international programs, reducing those services; the House cleared it 214-212, the Senate 51-48.
siblingLines.free_speech: Ended federal funding for NPR and PBS member stations; the House cleared it 214-212, the Senate 51-48.

rows.why: Sec. 2(b) rescinds unobligated balances for Contributions to International Organizations and peacekeeping, which are State Department accounts: the act’s cut_spending line (“Cancelled unobligated balances for the State Department, USAID and public broadcasting”) already states them, so a line would restate a part of a sibling’s total.

rows.title: Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2021
rows.priorWhy: “Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2021” names its subject but not what it would change about background checks. (Recorded in db/vr-title-effect-lines.json; reread against the measure’s text on file, which changes nothing here.)

siblingLines.gun_safety: Would have extended background checks to the private-sale channel, routing unlicensed transfers through a licensed dealer.

rows.why: Sec. 3 routes unlicensed transfers through a dealer (gun_safety line); the remaining clauses are exceptions, a dealer notice/certification form supporting that regime, a penalty cross-reference, and rules of construction (no registry); no clearly separate gun-rights change.

rows.title: Public Education Reporting Amendments
rows.priorWhy: Provision only "mandates regular program reviews by the Education Interim Committee for certain programs"; nothing on disclosure, stock trading or ethics rules.
rows.provisions: This bill: mandates regular program reviews by the Education Interim Committee for certain programs; and makes technical changes.
rows.why: The only change adds five-year Education Interim Committee reviews of listed education programs (plus a conjunction edit); it adds no disclosure, trading ban, or ethics rule.

rows.title: Public Education Reporting Amendments
rows.priorWhy: The only operative provision is the Education Interim Committee program review, already stated on the transparency pair; the provisions do not say the programs are public school programs or change them.
rows.provisions: This bill: mandates regular program reviews by the Education Interim Committee for certain programs; and makes technical changes.
rows.why: The inserted Subsection (3) only schedules five-year Education Interim Committee reviews of programs such as the Teacher and Student Success Program; reviewing a program neither funds schools nor raises teacher pay.

rows.title: Housing and Transit Reinvestment Zone Amendments
rows.priorWhy: The provisions change zone size, affordability thresholds and tax increment capture; none states a change to transit service, and the increment change is on the other pair’s line.

siblingLines.housing: Required 12% of the homes proposed in a housing and transit reinvestment zone to be reserved for set income levels.
siblingLines.dev_district_finance: Limited a housing and transit reinvestment zone to one sales and use tax increment period and required it to be at least 10 acres.

rows.provisions: This bill: amends definitions related to housing and transit reinvestment zones; amends provisions related to affordable housing thresholds to require 12% of the proposed dwelling units be reserved for certain levels of income; requires affordable housing requirements be met in each phase of development; requires that a housing and transit reinvestment zone be at least 10 acres; clarifies notice requirements to certain entities regarding the commencement of collection of tax increment; clarifies information required in a housing and transit reinvestment zone proposal; adds two additional members of the Legislature to the housing and transit reinvestment zone committee; amends provisions regarding overlap of a housing and transit reinvestment zone with a community reinvestment project area; amends provisions related to the sales and use tax increment captured within a housing and transit reinvestment zone, including: how base year is established; contiguity of affected sales and use tax boundaries; and limiting a housing and transit reinvestment zone to only one sales and use tax increment period; amends the amount of housing and transit reinvestment zone funds allowed for administration of the housing and transit reinvestment zone; allows minor adjustments to a housing and transit reinvestment zone if the county assessor or county auditor adjusts parcel boundaries; and makes technical changes.
rows.why: Checked all inserts: affordability thresholds, density at transit hubs and BRT stations, light rail radius for two stations, 10-acre minimum and tax increment rules; these govern housing zones around transit, not transit service itself.

rows.title: Optometrist Practice Amendments
rows.priorWhy: The provisions create a state certification for optometrist laser procedures with training and reporting duties; nothing concerns federal regulations, so no faithful line fits this issue.
rows.provisions: This bill: creates a certification for an optometrist to perform certain laser procedures; requires an optometrist to obtain training to obtain the certification; requires a certified optometrist to comply with reporting requirements and other standards; requires the Office of Professional Licensure Review to make a recommendation after reviewing outcome data on whether optometrists should continue performing the laser procedures; and creates a sunset date.
rows.why: The bill creates a state optometrist laser-procedure certification with training, reporting and a sunset; no text mentions federal regulations or their review.

rows.title: Housing Affordability Modifications
rows.priorWhy: The first-time homebuyer provisions (lender rules and the shared appreciation loan program) are what the bill’s shipped Housing line already says; the insurance incentive is only a rule the corporation is directed to make, and is not tied to first-time buyers.

siblingLines.housing: Created a shared appreciation loan program and had the Utah Housing Corporation set rules for lenders of first-time homebuyer loans.
siblingLines.housing_support: Let counties and municipalities use home ownership promotion zone funds for water exaction, street lighting, and environmental remediation.

rows.provisions: This bill: defines terms; amends provisions allowing revenue from a home ownership promotion zone to be used for certain purposes; enacts provisions allowing legislative bodies to settle certain litigation through a consent agreement; allows a county and municipality to use home ownership promotion zone funds for all or part of water exaction, street lighting, and environmental remediation costs; requires a county to comply with land use provisions for all pending and new land use applications; directs the Utah Housing Corporation to make rules regarding: procedures, qualifications, and requirements for private financial institutions that offer certain mortgage loans to first-time homebuyers; and the creation of an incentive program for qualified buyers to assist certain borrowers with the purchase of liability insurance for certain qualifying projects; provides that first-time home buyers may use certain mortgage loans for specified purposes; creates a subordinate shared appreciation loan program to be administered by the Department of Workforce Services to assist borrowers for certain purposes; and makes technical and conforming changes.
rows.why: Read the First-Time Homebuyer Assistance Program and shared appreciation loan sections; the only other change there is a construction liability insurance incentive for qualified borrowers on condominium projects, a rule directive not tied to first-time buyers beyond the sibling line.

rows.title: Micro-education Entity Amendments
rows.priorWhy: The provisions concern facility occupancy and square footage rules and the definition of school; nothing in them changes parental say over curriculum or instruction.

siblingLines.school_choice: Removed certain square footage requirements and expanded facilities where a micro-education entity or home-based microschool may operate.

rows.provisions: This bill: expands the types of facilities in which a micro-education entity or home-based microschool may operate by expanding the sets of occupancy requirements the facility may satisfy; removes certain square footage requirements; and excludes a micro-education entity or home-based microschool from a definition of "school" that subjects schools to certain administrative regulations.
rows.why: Changes strike square footage rules, expand facility occupancy options, and exclude microschools from a health-code definition of school; none gives parents say over curriculum or materials.

rows.title: Judicial Amendments
rows.priorWhy: The bill changes who appoints the chief justice; it says nothing about court orders on executive action, which is this issue.
rows.provisions: This bill: modifies provisions governing the membership and internal management of the Supreme Court; provides that the governor shall appoint a chief justice of the Supreme Court (chief justice) when a vacancy in the office occurs; modifies provisions related to an interim chief justice and appointment procedures; requires that a governor's selection for chief justice is subject to the advice and consent of the Senate; and makes conforming changes.
rows.why: The only change moves chief justice selection to governor appointment with Senate consent and adjusts interim rules; nothing concerns court orders on executive action.

rows.title: A joint resolution to terminate the national emergency declared to impose duties on articles imported from Canada
rows.priorWhy: The rationale's one effect, removing the import taxes by ending the tariff emergency, is what the act's tariffs_prices line already says; the rest reports what supporters say about prices. (Recorded in db/vr-blank-rows-slice13.json; reread against the measure’s text on file, which changes nothing here.)

siblingLines.tariffs_prices: Would have ended the emergency behind the tariffs on Canadian imports, lifting those duties; the Senate passed it 51-48.

rows.why: Single clause terminating the Canada tariff emergency under the National Emergencies Act; that is the tariffs_prices line and nothing else in the text bears on prices.

rows.title: A joint resolution to direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from hostilities against the Islamic Republic of Iran that have not been authorized by Congress
rows.priorWhy: The rationale ("Concerns the scope and restraint of U.S. military involvement abroad") states a topic, not an effect; the act's one effect is already the iran_policy and strong_defense lines' subject. (Recorded in db/vr-blank-rows-slice13.json; reread against the measure’s text on file, which changes nothing here.)

siblingLines.iran_policy: Would have ordered U.S. forces out of hostilities against Iran that Congress had not authorized; the Senate refused to discharge it 47-53.
siblingLines.strong_defense: Would have pulled U.S. forces from Iran hostilities until Congress authorized them; the Senate refused to discharge it 47-53.

rows.why: Sec. 1 is findings; Sec. 2 directs termination of unauthorized Iran hostilities with a self-defense rule of construction, already the iran_policy/strong_defense lines; nothing on NATO, allies or diplomacy.
